page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. This configuration comprises 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance in specific multi-threaded and memory-intensive tasks. The instance achieves a strong rating in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 269.5 GB/sec and large-block read-only memory bandwidth at 209.21 GB/sec. PassMark CPU extended instructions and database operations also rank in the top 25% tier. Conversely, the instance exhibits average performance across standard compute metrics, including stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. Large-language model text generation speeds are relatively weak, registering at 56.49 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 8.69 tokens per second for a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfc6.16xlarge offers a high-density compute profile with dedicated CPU allocation, making it a viable option for CPU-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The high memory bandwidth for large blocks and strong database operation benchmarks suggest this instance is well-suited for relational database hosting, multi-threaded data decompression, and compute-heavy application servers. It is also appropriate for static web serving and software compilation, though it is less optimal for LLM text generation tasks.
